Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Rejections commonly result from missing priority and ship_country; qty was also missing in the Cy Reyes attempts.
- Do not infer or fabricate missing values. Extract values from the complete source record, preserving customer, email, and date accurately.
- Source excerpts may be truncated in the displayed prompt; avoid treating incomplete text as complete data. If required fields cannot be verified, leave them missing rather than guessing.
- A corrected resubmission can be accepted on attempt 2: Bo Okafor and Dee Reyes succeeded after initial rejection. Eli Okafor also succeeded on attempt 2.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 demonstrated this.
- Handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, and partner-portal origins do not by themselves determine validity; completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- For each submission, ensure all six required keys are present and correctly named (especially “priority,” not “prio”), with valid values before submitting.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use the required key “priority,” never “prio.”
- Version 2 also validates the listed fields and still requires a valid priority; do not assume version changes eliminate any field requirement.
- Rejections commonly involve missing/invalid priority and ship_country. ORD-5110–5114 repeatedly failed because these could not be verified; ORD-5115–5117 succeeded only after a corrected third attempt.
- Never infer or fabricate values. Extract customer, email, date, priority, quantity, and country from the complete source record, preserving exact values.
- Displayed excerpts and transcriptions may be truncated. Treat incomplete text as insufficient evidence; leave unverifiable fields missing rather than guessing or submitting them.
- A corrected resubmission may succeed on attempts 2 or 3 (Bo Okafor, Dee Reyes, Eli Okafor succeeded on attempt 2; Dee Sato succeeded on attempt 3).
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 and ORD-5110–5114 demonstrate this.
- Origin or routing (handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, partner portal, or front desk) does not determine validity. Completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- Before submission, confirm all six listed keys are present, correctly named, and populated with valid, source-supported values.

Order intake notes:
- Versions 1 and 2 require exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.” Version 2 does not relax any requirement.
- Populate every key with valid, exact, source-supported values. Never infer, fabricate, or substitute values based on labels such as “ordinary priority.”
- Excerpts, pasted records, and transcriptions can be truncated. If priority, qty, ship_country, or any other field is incomplete or unverifiable, do not guess or submit; obtain the complete source or leave it for review.
- Recent failures confirm that truncated records repeatedly fail validation: ORD-5120–5123 failed on priority; ORD-5124–5126 failed on priority and qty; ORD-5127–5129 failed on priority. Repeating a submission without new complete evidence will not fix it.
- Corrected resubmissions can succeed on attempts 2 or 3, but only when missing/invalid values are actually corrected. Track attempts per order.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, and ORD-5129 reached that limit; do not make a fourth attempt.
- Intake origin or routing (front desk, partner portal, voicemail, email, handwritten, or transcribed) does not determine validity. Completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- Before submission, verify all six required keys are present, correctly named, populated, and supported by the complete source record.

Order intake notes:
- Versions 1–2 require exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Version 3 requires exactly six keys: cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty. Do not submit ship_country for version 3; do not submit extra fields.
- Every value must be exact, valid, and supported by the complete source. Never infer priority from “ordinary priority,” labels, routing notes, or other descriptions.
- Truncated transcriptions, pasted excerpts, voicemail fragments, and system/error responses are not complete source records. If any required field—especially priority or qty—is missing, invalid, or unverifiable, obtain the complete source or leave the order for review.
- Invalid priority repeatedly causes rejection. ORD-5130, ORD-5132–5133, ORD-5135–5139 demonstrate that resubmitting unchanged or using an error response does not fix the record. ORD-5131 succeeded only after correction; corrected retries can succeed when actual missing/invalid values are fixed.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review; never make a fourth attempt. ORD-5120, 5123, 5126, 5129, 5134, and 5137 reached that limit.
- Intake origin, forwarding person, duplicate-check claim, and routing (front desk, portal, voicemail, email, handwritten, or transcription) do not determine validity. Validate field names and source support.
- Before every submission, verify the applicable version’s six keys are present, correctly named, populated, and supported by the complete original record. Do not treat returned JSON, status, error, reason, or order_id fields as order-source values.

Order intake notes:
- Versions 1–2 require exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Version 3 requires exactly six keys: cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty. Do not submit ship_country or extra fields.
- Version 4 forms observed the same six-key layout as version 3: cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty. Treat all six as required; do not assume version 4 changes validation rules.
- Every value must be exact, valid, and supported by the complete original source. Never infer priority from “ordinary priority,” intake labels, routing notes, or other descriptions. Do not infer qty or destination from incomplete context.
- Truncated transcriptions, pasted excerpts, voicemail fragments, and system/error responses are not complete source records. If any required value—especially priority, qty, or destination—is missing, invalid, or unverifiable, obtain the complete source or leave the order for review.
- Invalid priority and qty repeatedly cause rejection. ORD-5130, ORD-5132–5133, ORD-5135–5139, ORD-5144–5148 show that resubmitting unchanged or using error responses does not fix records. Corrected retries can succeed only when actual missing/invalid source values are fixed.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review; never make a fourth attempt. ORD-5120, 5123, 5126, 5129, 5134, 5137, 5140, 5143, 5146, and 5149 reached that limit.
- Intake origin, forwarding person, duplicate-check claim, and routing do not determine validity.
- Before every submission, verify the applicable six keys, exact names, populated values, and support in the complete original record. Never submit returned JSON fields such as status, reason, action, order, or order_id.

Order intake notes:
- Versions 1–2 require exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Versions 3–4 require exactly six keys: cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty. Do not include ship_country or any extra fields.
- Every value must be exact, valid, and supported by the complete original source. Never infer priority from “ordinary priority,” intake labels, routing notes, or similar descriptions. Never infer qty, destination, customer, or other values from incomplete context.
- Phone-order transcriptions, voicemail excerpts, handwritten-order transcriptions, pasted email excerpts, and system/error responses are not complete source records. Missing or unverifiable destination, priority, qty, customer, email, or other required data requires obtaining the complete source or manual review.
- Version 4 cases repeatedly failed with missing destination and qty; incomplete customer transcriptions also caused rejection. A later retry succeeds only if the actual source defect is corrected.
- Do not treat intake origin, forwarding person, partner-portal claim, “duplicate check done,” or customer confirmation wording as validation or evidence of missing fields.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review; never make a fourth attempt. Orders reaching the limit include ORD-5120, 5123, 5126, 5129, 5134, 5137, 5140, 5143, 5146, 5149, 5152, 5155, and 5158.
- Before every submission, verify the applicable six keys, exact names, populated values, and support in the complete original record.
- Submit only those six order fields. Never submit returned JSON fields such as status, reason, action, order, order_id, review, or other response metadata.
